summary: Hanchi Wang, a software engineer lead at Azure AI (Microsoft), presents Azure AI Studio and Prompt Flow as complementary tools for building custom copilot solutions. He notes that while 2023 was the year the world discovered generative AI, 2024 is when organizations began deriving business value. He emphasizes AI is not plug-and-play—LLMs must integrate with domain knowledge and tools, outputs must be filtered for safety, and deployed applications require continuous monitoring. Azure AI Studio is the development hub hosting AI services, models, cognitive capabilities, search, ML, and full LLM Ops management, with over 20,000 monthly enterprise customers. Prompt Flow complements it as a 100% open-source SDK and VS Code extension for building, testing, tracing, and evaluating applications. Three superpowers are highlighted: tracing/instrumentation, evaluation, and monitoring. A chatbot demo for an outdoor equipment company uses the Assistant API with SQL generation and code interpreter tools. Prompt Flow's trace decorator captures inputs, outputs, and LLM interactions, viewable locally or in AI Studio. For evaluation, Wang shows built-in content safety evaluators and custom evaluators for execution time, error rate, and SQL similarity. He demonstrates model comparison across multiple models (GPT-3.5 Turbo, Mistral Large, GPT-4 Turbo) using the same custom dataset, revealing tradeoffs between speed and accuracy. For production monitoring, Prompt Flow's OpenTelemetry-based traces are collected in Azure Application Insights, with dashboards showing performance, usage, and failure metrics. The demo reveals the LLM produced an incorrect chart, underscoring the importance of evaluation and monitoring throughout the application lifecycle.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

takeaways: Azure AI Studio is the development hub for AI applications, now GA with over 20,000 monthly enterprise customers
Prompt Flow is a 100% open-source SDK and VS Code extension complementing AI Studio for building, testing, tracing, and evaluating AI applications
Three key superpowers are highlighted: tracing/instrumentation, evaluation, and monitoring
The trace decorator captures inputs, outputs, and LLM interactions using OpenTelemetry standards, enabling integration with existing observability tools like Azure Application Insights
Evaluation supports built-in content safety evaluators and custom evaluators, with model comparison across different models using the same custom dataset
Model comparison reveals tradeoffs between speed and accuracy—e.g., GPT-4 Turbo was slowest but had the highest SQL similarity score
Production monitoring dashboards show performance, usage, and failure metrics, with the ability to drill into individual traces for debugging
Token usage analysis can reveal cost optimization opportunities, such as shortening prompt templates when most tokens are used for prompts
Even well-constructed chatbot demos can produce incorrect results, underscoring the need for continuous evaluation and monitoring

sections.title: Introduction and Context
sections.summary: Hanchi Wang introduces himself and frames the talk around enterprise AI adoption in 2024. He notes that AI requires integration with domain knowledge, content safety filtering, and continuous monitoring, and introduces Azure AI Studio and Prompt Flow as Microsoft's tools for building AI applications.

sections.title: Azure AI Studio and Prompt Flow Overview
sections.summary: Describes Azure AI Studio as the development hub with AI services, models, ML capabilities, and trust/safety tools, now GA with 20,000+ monthly enterprise customers. Prompt Flow is a 100% open-source SDK and VS Code extension for end-to-end development, free for local use but more powerful with AI Studio. Three superpowers are highlighted: tracing, evaluation, and monitoring.

sections.title: Chatbot Demo
sections.summary: Demonstrates a chatbot app for an outdoor equipment company that answers sales-data questions using the Assistant API with two tools: SQL query generation from natural language and a code interpreter for charting. The demo shows a follow-up question producing an incorrect chart, underscoring the need for evaluation and monitoring. A sequence diagram is shown.

sections.title: Tracing and Instrumentation
sections.summary: Shows the chatbot code with Prompt Flow's trace decorator that captures inputs, outputs, and LLM interactions automatically. Demonstrates the local UI via 'pf flow test' command, with drill-down into tool calls and LLM traces. Notes that all instrumentation uses OpenTelemetry standards, enabling integration with existing observability infrastructure. Traces can be viewed in Azure AI Studio and shared via URL.

sections.title: Evaluation Capabilities
sections.summary: Covers evaluation for application quality, emphasizing the non-deterministic nature of LLMs and the need for high-quality test datasets. Shows the evaluate function from Prompt Flow, with a built-in content safety evaluator and custom evaluators for execution time, error rate, and SQL similarity scores. Mentions that evaluation results can be viewed in the terminal or in Azure AI Studio.

sections.title: Model Comparison and Production Monitoring
sections.summary: Demonstrates viewing aggregated evaluation results in Azure AI Studio, including content safety metrics and per-row traces. Shows model comparison across GPT-3.5 Turbo, Mistral Large, and GPT-4 Turbo using the same custom dataset, revealing tradeoffs between speed and accuracy. Covers the third superpower—production monitoring—using Azure Application Insights to collect OpenTelemetry traces, with dashboards showing performance, usage, and failure metrics. Highlights insights such as GPT-4 Turbo being slowest (aligning with evaluation), majority of tokens used for prompts, and the ability to drill into individual traces for debugging.
